d4-writer-death: The script runs each FIFO test of the tree (collected test ids containing "fifo", from test files that call mkfifo) in its own pytest process. A sitecustomize module makes the test-owned FIFO writer end just before it opens the FIFO for writing: a writer in a child process exits with status 1, and a writer in a thread of the test process gets an I/O error. A reproduction means at least one of these FIFO tests was still running 150 seconds after it started and was killed.
d4-writer-stall: The script runs each FIFO test of the tree (collected test ids containing "fifo", from test files that call mkfifo) in its own pytest process. A sitecustomize module makes a test-owned FIFO writer in a child process open the FIFO for writing and then sleep, holding the descriptor open and writing nothing. A reproduction means at least one of these FIFO tests was still running 150 seconds after it started and was killed.
d4-writer-startup: The script runs each FIFO test of the tree (collected test ids containing "fifo", from test files that call mkfifo) in its own pytest process. When a test starts a Python writer whose -c code opens a file in "wb" mode, the writer is replaced by one that sleeps for an hour before reading its standard input, so a large payload the test writes to the writer's stdin, or the test's read of the writer's readiness line, blocks. A reproduction means at least one of these FIFO tests was still running 60 seconds after it started and was killed.
f10-one-process-two-apps: The script creates two app instances with the tree's exported createApp in one Node process, both given the same temporary copy of the seeded data file, and sends one POST /items to each instance at the same time, for up to 20 rounds. After each round it reads the file and looks for every item that was answered 201. A reproduction means an item answered 201 was missing from the file.
f10-one-process-path-alias: The script creates two app instances with the tree's exported createApp in one Node process; the first names a temporary copy of the seeded data file by its absolute path and the second names the same file by a relative path. It sends one POST /items to each instance at the same time, for up to 20 rounds, and after each round reads the file and looks for every item that was answered 201. A reproduction means an item answered 201 was missing from the file.
f10-nonobject-items-file: The script starts the tree's app on a temporary copy of the seeded data file and sends POST /items with JSON bodies that are not objects: null, 5, "text", true and [1]. For each it compares the response with status 400 and the body {error: 'invalid_body', field: 'name'}. A reproduction means at least one of these bodies got a different response.
d3-executable-delimiter: The script builds a parent program with the tree's Command whose child subcommand is a real executable script, reached directly, through an alias, as the default command and as a nested command, and runs it with -- followed by option-like words such as --not-an-option. It compares what the spawned child received with the -- and the words after it kept as operands in their order, later -- tokens included, and no options set. A reproduction means at least one of the five cases gave the child different arguments or options, or the child did not exit 0.
d3-regression-child-probe: The script runs the tree's own test named "executable delimiter: help command still invokes child help" in tests/command.executableSubcommand.test.js with node --test, allowing it 18 seconds. A reproduction means that test failed with a spawn timeout (ETIMEDOUT) while the test file starts its child through node --eval.
